sections.heading: Overview
sections.content: The Barbell Back Squat is a fundamental compound exercise that targets the lower body, primarily the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings. It's considered one of the most effective exercises for building overall lower body strength and mass.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content: Builds lower body strength and power. Increases muscle mass in legs and glutes. Improves core stability and balance. Enhances athletic performance. Increases bone density.

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content: Primary: Quadriceps. Secondary: Glutes, Hamstrings, Erector Spinae, Core.

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Position the barbell at upper chest height on the rack.
2. Step under the bar and position it on your upper back/traps.
3. Grip the bar with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
4. Unrack the bar and step back 2-3 steps.

sections.heading: Execution
sections.content:
1. Set your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly pointed out.
2. Brace your core and take a deep breath.
3. Initiate the movement by breaking at the hips and knees simultaneously.
4. Descend until thighs are parallel to the ground or lower.
5. Drive through your mid-foot and heels to stand back up.
6. Exhale at the top of the movement.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Knees caving inward
- Rounding the lower back
- Not reaching proper depth
- Lifting heels off the ground
- Looking up or down (keep neck neutral)

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Barbell
- Squat Rack or Power Rack
- Weight Plates
- Safety Bars/Spotter Arms (recommended)
- Lifting Belt (optional)
- Squat Shoes (optional)

sections.heading: Rack Setup
sections.content:
1. Set the J-hooks at upper chest height (easier to unrack).
2. Set safety bars just below your bottom squat position.
3. Load the barbell evenly on both sides.
4. Use collars to secure the plates.
5. Clear the area around the rack of any obstacles.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Bar Position: High bar (on traps) or Low bar (rear delts).
2. Grip: Thumbless or full grip, hands as close as comfortable.
3. Elbow Position: Down and back, creating upper back tension.
4. Stance: Feet shoulder-width, toes 15-30° out.
5. Core: Deep breath and brace before each rep.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Front Squat: Barbell held in front, more quad emphasis
- Goblet Squat: Dumbbell or kettlebell held at chest
- Bulgarian Split Squat: Single-leg variation
- Leg Press: Machine-based alternative
- Hack Squat: Machine squat variation

sections.heading: Progression/Regression
sections.content:
Easier: Bodyweight Squat, Box Squat, Wall Squat
Harder: Pause Squat, Tempo Squat, Front Squat

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Knee Issues: Try box squats, reduce depth
Back Issues: Front squat, goblet squat, or leg press
Mobility Issues: Goblet squat, elevated heel squat shoes
No Barbell: Dumbbell goblet squat, Bulgarian split squat
